newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit down on dollar covering, falls limited.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit down on dollar covering, falls limited.

text.p: The ringgit traded in a tight range against the dollar after slipping in early Asian trading on Monday as players covered their short dollar positions from last week, dealers said.
They said stop-loss dollar selling and talk of Bank Negara support for the ringgit limited the Malaysian unit's downside.

"Unlike last week, the market was extremely quiet today. It was a 20-point range all the way," said a Malaysian bank dealer. The ringgit had jumped sharply last week following a steep rise in tomorrow/next rates on talk Bank Negara had asked local banks to stop quoting rates to foreign parties.
Bank Negara denied it had issued instructions to banks to stop undertaking swap transactions.
News of a sharply higher-than-expected trade surplus for March also helped the ringgit's rise on Friday.
Dealers said tom/next rates had fallen back to more normal levels on Monday after trading as high as 300 on Friday.
The ringgit was quoted at 2.4930/40 a dollar at 0900 GMT against 2.4870/90 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Friday.
Some dealers said there was speculation that Bank Negara was supporting the ringgit at around 2.4950 as many Kuala Lumpur banks were offering dollars at that level.
Dealers said players also refrained from active participation ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday.
They said foreign funds were still trying to get out of their positions and the dollar would be sold on any rallies against the ringgit.
Given the current high short-term interbank rates, it would be too expensive for players to maintain short ringgit positions, they said.
Dealers expect dollar/ringgit to trade between 2.4800 and 2.5000 in the next few days.
